newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans on trial for kidnap of multi-millionaire.
newsitem.headline: Germans on trial for kidnap of multi-millionaire.

text.p: Two men went on trial on Thursday for the kidnapping of a Hamburg multimillionaire whose family paid the largest ransom in German criminal history.

Wolfgang Koszics and Peter Richter face several years in jail if convicted of helping to abduct Jan Philipp Reemstma, the former owner of Germany's second largest tobacco firm, from his home in March 1996.
Reemstma was released in return for 30 million marks ($19 million). Police are still hunting for most of the ransom and a man they suspect of masterminding the crime.
Richter and Koszics, who face charges of criminal extortion, were arrested in Spain last May and extradited to Germany.

Reemstma, who sold the family empire in 1980 and has since devoted much of his time and money to academic research and sponsorship of the arts, was held in the cellar of a cottage near the northern city of Bremen for five weeks.
Police imposed a news blackout and communicated with the kidnappers through the personal columns of a Hamburg newspaper.
